title: Demo request — vectorization scale & go-live window
text:
Demo request — vectorization scale & go-live window

["From: Samir Patel <samir@shopgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request — vectorization scale & go-live window

Hi Mina,

We signed up on the self-serve flow this morning (ShopGrid) and I'm the PM owning search. We're evaluating vectorized product search (embeddings + ANN) and want to understand how Redwood handles inference at scale. A few quick details: 

- Use case: product search relevancy + occasional personalization signals (mostly search).
- Current traffic: ~50k queries/day today, expected to grow to ~250k/day in peak months.
- Concurrency: peaks around 180–220 qps; average ~30 qps.
- Target latency: P95 < 150ms (ideally <100ms for search).
- Timeline: pilot in Q3 (30-day pilot), production target in Q4.

Can we do a 30-min technical demo to run through architecture, expected throughput, and a quick look at cost tradeoffs (batching, quantization)? Happy to include an engineer — I can share a small traffic sample.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Product Manager, ShopGrid
samir@shopgrid.com
+1 415-555-0142
", "From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@shopgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 16:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — vectorization scale & go-live window

Hi Samir — great to meet you and thanks for the context. Ben (cc'd) is our SDR who will coordinate scheduling. A couple of quick qualification questions so we can tailor the session and bring the right folks: 

1) Is the search workload single-shot (query -> vector lookup) or do you expect multi-stage rerank (candidate generation -> cross-encoder rerank)?
2) Which model(s) are you evaluating (open-source embeddings, hosted provider models, or a mix)?
3) Typical query length and average token size (just ballpark is fine)?
4) Do you plan to serve embeddings in a single region or multi-region for latency?
5) Any compliance constraints (PII, data residency) we should be aware of ahead of the demo?

If you can reply with short answers we will bake them into the demo deck. I attached a short pre-demo checklist that explains what info helps us (traffic sample format, representative queries, and an ideal test timeout). Once we have that, Ben will propose three slots.

Looking forward to it — 30 minutes is a good place to start.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-demo-checklist.pdf
", "From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@shopgrid.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Scheduling — 30 min demo (Redwood + ShopGrid)

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick reply earlier (Mina). Based on Mina's notes, here are three 30-minute slots (all PT) — pick whichever works and we'll send a calendar invite + join link: 

- Tue 2027-06-15, 10:00–10:30 PT
- Tue 2027-06-15, 14:00–14:30 PT
- Wed 2027-06-16, 09:00–09:30 PT

If those don't fit, tell me your timezone and a couple windows and we'll match. We'll have Mina on the call for architecture + throughput, and Connor (engineer) will join for any deep technical Qs about batching and KV caching.

Quick note on the agenda: 1) 5 min intros; 2) 15 min architecture & throughput discussion tailored to your traffic; 3) 10 min Q&A + next steps (pilot sizing).

Booking link (if easier): https://cal.example/book?slot=3

Cheers,
Ben Carter
SDR, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

--
Added to calendar: Connor O'Brien (eng) will be available for the preferred slot.
", "From: Samir Patel <samir@shopgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling — 30 min demo (Redwood + ShopGrid)

Perfect — thanks, Ben. Wed 2027-06-16 09:00 PT works for us. Please include our backend engineer Alicia (alicia@shopgrid.com) on the invite. I'm attaching a small traffic sample (first 24 hours of logs, sanitized) so you can see the qps distribution and typical query lengths.

Answers to Mina's questions:
1) Mostly single-shot candidate retrieval. We may add a light rerank step later but plan to pilot with retrieval-first.
2) Planning to use open-source embedding models (we're experimenting with two families).
3) Typical query tokens: 6–12 tokens; long-tail queries up to ~40 tokens.
4) Start single-region (us-west) but expect multi-region in 2028.
5) No special residency constraints for the pilot; everything is sanitized for the sample.

Attachment: shopgrid_sample_traffic.csv

See you on Wed.
Samir
